answers.text: Three lines, always the same order: drop-off time, pallet count, any damage noted. Every time, no exceptions.
Turn the week's calls into a list — time, customer, topic, outcome — and count how many need a follow-up call at the bottom.
Something about the timing in that note feels off, worth a second look before it's filed.
The invoice growth number looks bigger than a 20% rise to me.
Output 2 — you can see the actual ticket counts behind the 88%. Output 1 gives you nothing to check.
Email 2, it's got the real volume numbers. Email 1 doesn't say what it's even comparing against.
The agreement covers the client's name, billing contact, the rates, the retainer cap, the non-disclosure clause and the service scope.
I'd cross-check the totals before it goes out.
Step 1, reading the invoice, matters because a bad read carries through. But step 4 — sending automatically — is really where I'd put the gate, since that's the point you can't take back.
